video.title: 8 Weird Side Hustles That Are Actually Making Money

summary: Side Hustle Nation host Nick Loper and guest Deakin Hayes (Well Kept Wallet) run through a listicle of unusual side hustles: a single-function word unscrambler site, calculator sites, dealership car review videos, a cheese fortune-teller, dog birthday party planning, line dancing instruction, DoorDash chore-filming for AI training, and a personalised home-cook food marketplace idea. Deakin also shares his own Facebook content monetisation income ($3-4k/month), his Claude plus Supermetrics MCP ad-reporting workflow for his marketing agency, and a rap album. Key takeaway: niche down to be the 'best, worst or only', and many income claims are unverified second-hand figures.

speakers.name: Deakin Hayes
speakers.description: Founder of Well Kept Wallet; runs a small online marketing agency and Facebook content pages

ideas.name: Single-function utility site monetised with ads (Word Unscrambler)
ideas.one_liner: Simple tool sites (word unscrambler, port checker, syllable counter) that earn from search traffic and display ads.
ideas.business_model: Display advertising on high-traffic free tool pages
ideas.customer: Word-game players (Scrabble, Wordle, Words with Friends) searching for help
ideas.problem: Players want to find words from a set of letters
ideas.offer: Free web tool that unscrambles letters into words, supported by supporting content on game tips

pricing.notes: Revenue estimates third-party: up to 5-6 million USD per year

acquisition_channels.details: Targets search intent keywords with extra content (Wordle tips, Sudoku tips, Boggle strategy) to build content authority.

quote.text: it is clearly targeting some search intent types of keywords, like free games, like wortle, Sudoku tips for absolute beginners
quote.speaker: Nick Loper

ideas.delivery: Fully automated website; built by one person (Ramesh in India) in 2014 as a weekend project, portfolio now about 17 million monthly visitors.
unit_economics_claims: Ad income estimates up to 5-6 million USD per year, host says even 100k USD/month on low end

acquisition.how: SEO content and programmatic pages can be agent-generated; occasional human review.

onboarding.how: No onboarding; visitors use the tool.

uk_applicability.notes: Works identically in the UK; ad networks pay in GBP/USD. Google ranking competition and AI-search risk apply.

risks: Traffic estimates are third-party and unverified
Google algorithm updates or AI answers can remove demand
Highly competitive; early mover advantage dated 2014

quotes.text: it's absolutely something you could build with AI today. 100%.
quotes.speaker: Nick Loper

quotes.text: some estimates range as high as five or six million dollars a year from the traffic on this site built in 2014 by this guy, Ramesh in India
quotes.speaker: Nick Loper

ideas.name: AI-built niche calculator sites
ideas.one_liner: Build simple calculators (tax estimator, intermittent fasting, paint, concrete, sod, macro, calorie deficit, reading level, garage fit) and monetise via ads.
ideas.problem: People need quick answers for estimates and measurements

price_points.label: Reported earnings of an intermittent fasting calculator

acquisition_channels.details: Host builds a side hustle tax calculator page and adds content and internal links to try to rank.

ideas.delivery: Software built with AI coding tools; no ongoing labour.
unit_economics_claims: Intermittent fasting calculator reportedly earns 400 USD/month and is AI-built

acquisition.how: SEO page generation by agents with spot checks.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in UK; localise calculators (UK tax, metric units) and note UK ad RPMs are lower.

risks: Calculator queries increasingly answered directly by Google/AI

quotes.text: I found this intermittent fasting calculator, which is making a reported $400 a month and very clearly built with AI.
quotes.speaker: Nick Loper

ideas.name: Independent short-form car review videos for dealerships
ideas.one_liner: Quebec creator paid by dealerships to film honest TikTok car reviews.
ideas.business_model: Per-day fee from dealerships (B2B video production)
ideas.problem: Dealers need trusted content to drive showroom traffic
ideas.offer: Short-form honest reviews (good, bad and ugly) in French, filmed at dealerships

pricing.notes: Claim by Nick about a third party

acquisition_channels.details: TikTok account (parlons auto) with ~6,000 followers; B2B outreach to local dealerships.

ideas.delivery: Creator films reviews in person at dealer lots following a repeatable checklist (exterior, fit and finish, seats, amenities).

acquisition.how: B2B sales to local dealers largely human.

uk_applicability.notes: UK dealerships exist and would buy; must disclose paid sponsorship under ASA/CMA rules.

risks: Independence perceived as compromised by dealer payment

quotes.text: he gets hired by dealerships to make these short form videos
quotes.speaker: Nick Loper

tactics.name: Facebook content factory with VA and SOP
steps: Get approved for Facebook monetisation (around 10k followers; Deakin had 50-60k) by clicking the interest button
Write a brand SOP with filters (no debt promotion)
Have a VA use Canva templates to produce posts
Start with 1 post/day, double up on formats that work (e.g. sample budgets), scale to ~16/day
Use AI to generate content ideas and graphics
Use a reward app to track daily output (7 unique posts)

tactics.name: Closed-loop ad reporting via MCP
steps: Connect Google Ads/CallRail to CRM like Jobber
Match ad click to revenue per job
Ask Claude for best and worst ads and actions

tactics.name: Best, worst or only niche positioning
steps: Choose a niche where you can be the only provider
Pair with a gimmick that earns press

tools_mentioned.name: Supermetrics
tools_mentioned.purpose: MCP connector for ad data in Claude

warnings.warning: Relying on going viral is risky.

quote.text: that second step of going viral always makes me a little bit nervous
quote.speaker: Nick Loper

warnings.warning: Simple sites can be killed by Google updates (episodeguidetv.com).

lessons.lesson: Niche down to be best, worst or only in a market to stand out.
You only need to stay one step ahead of students to teach a skill.
Build a system for one platform before syndicating to others.
Early revenue is small; systems and SOPs make content creation sustainable.
Closing the loop between ad spend and revenue improves ad decisions.
Experience-based businesses are harder for AI to replace.

evidence_quality.rationale: Listicle of mostly second-hand, unverified income claims; Deakin's Facebook income is first-hand but unverified. Transcript is Whisper tiny.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sponsor reads for Quo, Gusto, Monarch and Shopify; Nick runs Side Hustle Nation and Deakin runs Well Kept Wallet.
